sanskrit: dantavakraḥ karūṣaś ca kalabho meghavāhanaḥ mūrdhnā divyaṃ maṇiṃ bibhrad yaṃ taṃ bhūtamaṇiṃ viduḥ
english: Dantavakra, Karūṣa, Kalabha, and Meghavāhana — bearing on their heads the divine jewel which is known as the bhūtamaṇi.

sanskrit: muraṃ ca narakaṃ caiva śāsti yo yavanādhipau aparyantabalo rājā pratīcyāṃ varuṇo yathā
english: And he rules over Mura and Naraka, the two lords of the Yavanas — a king of boundless power in the west, like Varuṇa himself.

sanskrit: bhagadatto mahārāja vṛddhas tava pituḥ sakhā sa vācā praṇatas tasya karmaṇā caiva bhārata
english: Bhagadatta, O great king, an old man and a friend of your father — he bows to Jarāsandha in word and in deed, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: snehabaddhas tu pitṛvan manasā bhaktimāṃs tvayi pratīcyāṃ dakṣiṇaṃ cāntaṃ pṛthivyāḥ pāti yo nṛpaḥ
english: Yet bound by affection, he is devoted to you in his heart like a father — and the king who guards the southern end of the west of the earth.

sanskrit: mātulo bhavataḥ śūraḥ purujit kuntivardhanaḥ sa te saṃnatimān ekaḥ snehataḥ śatrutāpanaḥ
english: Your maternal uncle, the valiant Purujit Kuntivardhana — he alone submits to you out of affection, O scorcher of enemies.

sanskrit: jarāsaṃdhaṃ gatas tv evaṃ purā yo na mayā hataḥ puruṣottamavijñāto yo 'sau cediṣu durmatiḥ
english: Having thus gone over to Jarāsandha, there is one whom I did not slay before — the evil-minded one in the Cedi country who is known as the foremost of men.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ pratijānāti loke 'smin puruṣottamam ādatte satataṃ mohād yaḥ sa cihnaṃ ca māmakam
english: He proclaims himself to be the foremost of men in this world and, deluded, constantly appropriates my own insignia as well.

sanskrit: vaṅgapuṇḍrakirāteṣu rājā balasamanvitaḥ pauṇḍrako vāsudeveti yo 'sau lokeṣu viśrutaḥ
english: Among the Vaṅgas, Puṇḍras, and Kirātas there is a king endowed with strength — that Pauṇḍraka who is renowned in the world as Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: caturyuḥ sa mahārāja bhoja indrasakho balī vidyābalād yo vyajayat pāṇḍyakrathakakaiśikān
english: He is endowed with four types of strength, O great king — a Bhoja, a friend of Indra, powerful, who by the strength of his knowledge conquered the Pāṇḍyas, Krathas, and Kaiśikas.

sanskrit: bhrātā yasyāhṛtiḥ śūro jāmadagnyasamo yudhi sa bhakto māgadhaṃ rājā bhīṣmakaḥ paravīrahā
english: Whose brother Āhṛti is a hero equal to Jāmadagnya in battle — that king Bhīṣmaka, slayer of enemy heroes, is devoted to the Māgadha king.

sanskrit: priyāṇy ācarataḥ prahvān sadā saṃbandhinaḥ sataḥ bhajato na bhajaty asmān apriyeṣu vyavasthitaḥ
english: He always acts agreeably toward his relations who bow before him — he who worships him does not honor us, being fixed in hostility toward us.

sanskrit: na kulaṃ na balaṃ rājann abhijānaṃs tathātmanaḥ paśyamāno yaśo dīptaṃ jarāsaṃdham upāśritaḥ
english: Not recognizing his own lineage or strength, O king, yet seeing his blazing fame, he has taken refuge with Jarāsandha.

sanskrit: udīcyabhojāś ca tathā kulāny aṣṭādaśābhibho jarāsaṃdhabhayād eva pratīcīṃ diśam āśritāḥ
english: And thus eighteen northern Bhoja clans, O lord, have sought refuge in the western direction out of fear of Jarāsandha.

sanskrit: śūrasenā bhadrakārā bodhāḥ śālvāḥ paṭaccarāḥ sustharāś ca sukuṭṭāś ca kuṇindāḥ kuntibhiḥ saha
english: The Śūrasenas, Bhadrakāras, Bodhas, Śālvas, Paṭaccaras, Sustharas, Sukuṭṭas, Kuṇindas together with the Kuntis —

sanskrit: śālveyānāṃ ca rājānaḥ sodaryānucaraiḥ saha dakṣiṇā ye ca pāñcālāḥ pūrvāḥ kuntiṣu kośalāḥ
english: And the kings of the Śālveyas with their brothers and followers, the southern Pāñcālas, those in the east among the Kuntis, the Kośalas —

sanskrit: tathottarāṃ diśaṃ cāpi parityajya bhayārditāḥ matsyāḥ saṃnyastapādāś ca dakṣiṇāṃ diśam āśritāḥ
english: And likewise, tormented by fear, abandoning the northern direction, the Matsyas and the Saṃnyastapādas have sought the southern direction.

sanskrit: tathaiva sarvapāñcālā jarāsaṃdhabhayārditāḥ svarāṣṭraṃ saṃparityajya vidrutāḥ sarvatodiśam
english: Similarly all the Pāñcālas, tormented by fear of Jarāsandha, have abandoned their own kingdoms and fled in all directions.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya kaṃso nirmathya bāndhavān bārhadrathasute devyāv upāgacchad vṛthāmatiḥ
english: Then after some time, Kaṃsa — crushing his kinsmen, the foolish one — came to the two daughters of the son of Bṛhadratha.

sanskrit: astiḥ prāptiś ca nāmnā te sahadevānuje 'bale balena tena sa jñātīn abhibhūya vṛthāmatiḥ
english: Those two were named Asti and Prāpti, younger sisters of Sahadeva — weak women. With that power, that fool overcame his kinsmen.

sanskrit: śraiṣṭhyaṃ prāptaḥ sa tasyāsīd atīvāpanayo mahān bhojarājanyavṛddhais tu pīḍyamānair durātmanā
english: He had attained supremacy — that was an exceedingly great wrong — while the elders among the Bhoja kings and nobles were being oppressed by that evil-souled one.

sanskrit: jñātitrāṇam abhīpsadbhir asmatsaṃbhāvanā kṛtā dattvākrūrāya sutanuṃ tām āhukasutāṃ tadā
english: By those who desired protection of their kinsmen, honor was shown to us — giving at that time the fair-bodied daughter of Āhuka's son to Akrūra.

sanskrit: saṃkarṣaṇadvitīyena jñātikāryaṃ mayā kṛtam hatau kaṃsasunāmānau mayā rāmeṇa cāpy uta
english: The duty to my kinsmen was fulfilled by me, accompanied by Saṃkarṣaṇa — Kaṃsa and Sunāman were slain by me and by Rāma as well.

sanskrit: bhaye tu samupakrānte jarāsaṃdhe samudyate mantro 'yaṃ mantrito rājan kulair aṣṭādaśāvaraiḥ
english: But when fear arose and Jarāsandha rose up in arms, this counsel was deliberated, O king, by the eighteen lesser clans together.

sanskrit: anāramanto nighnanto mahāstraiḥ śataghātibhiḥ na hanyāma vayaṃ tasya tribhir varṣaśatair balam
english: Even striking relentlessly with great weapons that kill by the hundreds, we could not destroy his army in three hundred years.

sanskrit: tasya hy amarasaṃkāśau balena balināṃ varau nāmabhyāṃ haṃsaḍibhakāv ity āstāṃ yodhasattamau
english: For in his army there were two foremost of warriors, equal to immortals in strength, the best among the mighty — known by the names Haṃsa and Ḍibhaka.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau sahitau vīrau jarāsaṃdhaś ca vīryavān trayas trayāṇāṃ lokānāṃ paryāptā iti me matiḥ
english: Those two heroes together and the valiant Jarāsandha — those three are sufficient for the three worlds, in my judgment.

sanskrit: na hi kevalam asmākaṃ yāvanto 'nye ca pārthivāḥ tathaiva teṣām āsīc ca buddhir buddhimatāṃ vara
english: Not only we, but all other kings as well — the wise among the wise held the same opinion about them.

sanskrit: atha haṃsa iti khyātaḥ kaś cid āsīn mahān nṛpaḥ sa cānyaiḥ sahito rājan saṃgrāme 'ṣṭādaśāvaraiḥ
english: Now there was a certain great king known as Haṃsa, and he along with others, O king, in battle with the eighteen lesser clans —

sanskrit: hato haṃsa iti proktam atha kenāpi bhārata tac chrutvā ḍibhako rājan yamunāmbhasy amajjata
english: "Haṃsa has been slain" — so it was said by someone, O Bhārata. Hearing that, O king, Ḍibhaka submerged himself in the waters of the Yamunā.

sanskrit: vinā haṃsena loke 'smin nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe ity etāṃ matim āsthāya ḍibhako nidhanaṃ gataḥ
english: "Without Haṃsa in this world I cannot bear to live" — with this resolve, Ḍibhaka met his end.

sanskrit: tathā tu ḍibhakaṃ śrutvā haṃsaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ prapede yamunām eva so 'pi tasyāṃ nyamajjata
english: Having heard of Ḍibhaka's death, Haṃsa — the conqueror of enemy cities — himself also entered the Yamunā and drowned in it.

sanskrit: tau sa rājā jarāsaṃdhaḥ śrutvāpsu nidhanaṃ gatau svapuraṃ śūrasenānāṃ prayayau bharatarṣabha
english: Hearing that those two had perished in the waters, king Jarāsandha departed to his own city of the Śūrasenas, O bull among Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tato vayam amitraghna tasmin pratigate nṛpe punar ānanditāḥ sarve mathurāyāṃ vasāmahe
english: Then, O slayer of enemies, when that king had withdrawn, we all rejoiced and resided again in Mathurā.

sanskrit: yadā tv abhyetya pitaraṃ sā vai rājīvalocanā kaṃsabhāryā jarāsaṃdhaṃ duhitā māgadhaṃ nṛpam
english: But when that lotus-eyed wife of Kaṃsa, his daughter, approached her father, king Jarāsandha of Māgadha —

sanskrit: codayaty eva rājendra pativyasanaduḥkhitā patighnaṃ me jahīty evaṃ punaḥ punar ariṃdama
english: Grieving over her husband's calamity, she urges him on, O king of kings — "Slay the killer of my husband!" — thus again and again, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: tato vayaṃ mahārāja taṃ mantraṃ pūrvamantritam saṃsmaranto vimanaso vyapayātā narādhipa
english: Then, O great king, remembering that counsel we had deliberated before, we departed in distress, O lord of men.

sanskrit: pṛthaktvena drutā rājan saṃkṣipya mahatīṃ śriyam prapatāmo bhayāt tasya sadhanajñātibāndhavāḥ
english: We fled separately, O king, abandoning our great prosperity — fleeing in fear of him, along with our wealth, kinsmen, and relations.

sanskrit: iti saṃcintya sarve sma pratīcīṃ diśam āśritāḥ kuśasthalīṃ purīṃ ramyāṃ raivatenopaśobhitām
english: Thinking thus, we all sought the western direction and the lovely city of Kuśasthalī, beautified by Mount Raivataka.

sanskrit: punar niveśanaṃ tasyāṃ kṛtavanto vayaṃ nṛpa tathaiva durgasaṃskāraṃ devair api durāsadam
english: We established our dwelling there again, O king, and likewise fortified it in a manner difficult to approach even by the gods.

sanskrit: striyo 'pi yasyāṃ yudhyeyuḥ kiṃ punar vṛṣṇipuṃgavāḥ tasyāṃ vayam amitraghna nivasāmo 'kutobhayāḥ
english: In that city even women could fight — how much more the foremost of Vṛṣṇis! We dwell there, O slayer of foes, without fear from any quarter.

sanskrit: ālokya girimukhyaṃ taṃ mādhavītīrtham eva ca mādhavāḥ kuruśārdūla parāṃ mudam avāpnuvan
english: Beholding that foremost of mountains and the tīrtha sacred to the Mādhavīs, the Mādhavakas, O tiger among Kurus, attained the highest joy.

sanskrit: evaṃ vayaṃ jarāsaṃdhād āditaḥ kṛtakilbiṣāḥ sāmarthyavantaḥ saṃbandhād bhavantaṃ samupāśritāḥ
english: Thus we, originally wronged by Jarāsandha, though possessed of power, have through kinship sought refuge with you.

sanskrit: triyojanāyataṃ sadma triskandhaṃ yojanād adhi yojanānte śatadvāraṃ vikramakramatoraṇam aṣṭādaśāvarair naddhaṃ kṣatriyair yuddhadurmadaiḥ
english: His abode extends three yojanas, is three-storied and more than a yojana high, has a hundred gates at each yojana's end, with successive arches of might, and is garrisoned by eighteen ranks of kṣatriyas frenzied for battle.

sanskrit: aṣṭādaśa sahasrāṇi vrātānāṃ santi naḥ kule āhukasya śataṃ putrā ekaikas triśatāvaraḥ
english: Eighteen thousand warriors of our clan there are; Āhuka has a hundred sons, each attended by no fewer than three hundred.

sanskrit: cārudeṣṇaḥ saha bhrātrā cakradevo 'tha sātyakiḥ ahaṃ ca rauhiṇeyaś ca sāmbaḥ śaurisamo yudhi
english: Cārudeṣṇa with his brother, Cakradeva, and Sātyaki; and I, and Rauhiṇeya, and Sāmba — equal to Śauri in battle —

sanskrit: evam ete rathāḥ sapta rājann anyān nibodha me kṛtavarmā anādhṛṣṭiḥ samīkaḥ samitiṃjayaḥ
english: These seven chariot-warriors, O king — now hear of others from me: Kṛtavarmā, Anādhṛṣṭi, Śamīka, and Samitiṃjaya —

sanskrit: kahvaḥ śaṅkur nidāntaś ca saptaivaite mahārathāḥ putrau cāndhakabhojasya vṛddho rājā ca te daśa
english: Kahva, Śaṅku, and Nidānta — these seven too are great chariot-warriors; the two sons of the Andhaka-Bhoja and the old king — those ten.

sanskrit: lokasaṃhananā vīrā vīryavanto mahābalāḥ smaranto madhyamaṃ deśaṃ vṛṣṇimadhye gatavyathāḥ
english: Heroes built like the pillars of the world, valiant and greatly powerful — remembering the middle country, they are afflicted with grief even among the Vṛṣṇis.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ samrāḍguṇair yuktaḥ sadā bharatasattama kṣatre samrājam ātmānaṃ kartum arhasi bhārata
english: You, endowed with the qualities of an emperor, O best among Bhāratas, you deserve to make yourself sovereign over the kṣatriyas, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: na tu śakyaṃ jarāsaṃdhe jīvamāne mahābale rājasūyas tvayā prāptum eṣā rājan matir mama
english: But it is not possible for you to accomplish the Rājasūya while Jarāsandha of great power still lives — this is my view, O king.

sanskrit: tena ruddhā hi rājānaḥ sarve jitvā girivraje kandarāyāṃ girīndrasya siṃheneva mahādvipāḥ
english: For by him all those kings have been imprisoned after being conquered at Girivraja — in the mountain cave, like great elephants by a lion.

sanskrit: so 'pi rājā jarāsaṃdho yiyakṣur vasudhādhipaiḥ ārādhya hi mahādevaṃ nirjitās tena pārthivāḥ
english: That king Jarāsandha too, wishing to sacrifice with the lords of the earth, propitiated Mahādeva — and those kings were conquered by him.

sanskrit: sa hi nirjitya nirjitya pārthivān pṛtanāgatān puram ānīya baddhvā ca cakāra puruṣavrajam
english: For he, conquering again and again the kings who came with their armies, brought them to his city, bound them, and made a pen of men.

sanskrit: vayaṃ caiva mahārāja jarāsaṃdhabhayāt tadā mathurāṃ saṃparityajya gatā dvāravatīṃ purīm
english: And we too, O great king, out of fear of Jarāsandha at that time abandoned Mathurā and went to the city of Dvāravatī.

sanskrit: yadi tv enaṃ mahārāja yajñaṃ prāptum ihecchasi yatasva teṣāṃ mokṣāya jarāsaṃdhavadhāya ca
english: But if, O great king, you wish to attain this sacrifice, then strive for the liberation of those kings and for the slaying of Jarāsandha.

sanskrit: samārambho hi śakyo 'yaṃ nānyathā kurunandana rājasūyasya kārtsnyena kartuṃ matimatāṃ vara
english: For this undertaking is possible in no other way, O joy of the Kurus — to fully perform the Rājasūya, O best of the wise.

sanskrit: ity eṣā me matī rājan yathā vā manyase 'nagha evaṃ gate mamācakṣva svayaṃ niścitya hetubhiḥ
english: This is my view, O king — or as you yourself think best, O sinless one, in this situation, declare it, having resolved it with your own reasoning.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca uktaṃ tvayā buddhimatā yan nānyo vaktum arhati saṃśayānāṃ hi nirmoktā tvan nānyo vidyate bhuvi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What you have spoken, O wise one, no other is worthy to speak — for there is no other on earth who can resolve doubts as you can.

sanskrit: gṛhe gṛhe hi rājānaḥ svasya svasya priyaṃkarāḥ na ca sāmrājyam āptās te samrāṭśabdo hi kṛtsnabhāk
english: In every household kings perform what is pleasing to themselves — but they have not attained sovereignty, for the title "emperor" encompasses all.

sanskrit: kathaṃ parānubhāvajñaḥ svaṃ praśaṃsitum arhati pareṇa samavetas tu yaḥ praśastaḥ sa pūjyate
english: How can one who knows the greatness of others praise himself? He who is praised in the company of his peers — he is truly honored.

sanskrit: viśālā bahulā bhūmir bahuratnasamācitā dūraṃ gatvā vijānāti śreyo vṛṣṇikulodvaha
english: The earth is vast and abundant, filled with many jewels — one learns what is best by going far, O chief of the Vṛṣṇi clan.

sanskrit: śamam eva paraṃ manye na tu mokṣād bhavec chamaḥ ārambhe pārameṣṭhyaṃ tu na prāpyam iti me matiḥ
english: I consider tranquility to be supreme — yet there is no tranquility apart from liberation. But sovereignty through undertaking is not to be attained — this is my view.

sanskrit: evam evābhijānanti kule jātā manasvinaḥ kaś cit kadā cid eteṣāṃ bhavec chreṣṭho janārdana
english: Thus those of noble birth who are high-minded understand — among them, someone at some time may become the foremost, O Janārdana.

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca anārambhaparo rājā valmīka iva sīdati durbalaś cānupāyena balinaṃ yo 'dhitiṣṭhati
english: Bhīma said: A king devoted to inaction sinks like an anthill. And he who faces a powerful enemy without proper means is weak indeed.

sanskrit: atandritas tu prāyeṇa durbalo balinaṃ ripum jayet samyaṅ nayo rājan nītyārthān ātmano hitān
english: Yet the vigilant one, though weak, can generally defeat a powerful enemy — through right policy, O king, understanding the ends of statecraft for his own benefit.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇe nayo mayi balaṃ jayaḥ pārthe dhanaṃjaye māgadhaṃ sādhayiṣyāmo vayaṃ traya ivāgnayaḥ
english: In Kṛṣṇa is wisdom, in me is strength, victory is in Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya — we three shall accomplish the Māgadha's defeat, like the three fires.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa uvāca ādatte 'rthaparo bālo nānubandham avekṣate tasmād ariṃ na mṛṣyanti bālam arthaparāyaṇam
english: Kṛṣṇa said: A foolish man intent on gain does not consider the consequences — therefore those who are intent on gain do not tolerate an enemy who is foolish.

sanskrit: hitvā karān yauvanāśvaḥ pālanāc ca bhagīrathaḥ kārtavīryas tapoyogād balāt tu bharato vibhuḥ ṛddhyā maruttas tān pañca samrāja iti śuśrumaḥ
english: Yauvanāśva through renouncing tributes, Bhagīratha through protection, Kārtavīrya through the practice of austerities, the mighty Bharata through strength, and Marutta through prosperity — these five we have heard of as emperors.

sanskrit: nigrāhyalakṣaṇaṃ prāpto dharmārthanayalakṣaṇaiḥ bārhadratho jarāsaṃdhas tad viddhi bharatarṣabha
english: Jarāsandha, son of Bṛhadratha, has acquired the marks of one to be subdued as indicated by the marks of dharma, artha, and policy — know this, O bull among Bhāratas.

sanskrit: na cainam anurudhyante kulāny ekaśataṃ nṛpāḥ tasmād etad balād eva sāmrājyaṃ kurute 'dya saḥ
english: And one hundred and one clans of kings do not follow him willingly — therefore he now maintains this sovereignty by force alone.

sanskrit: ratnabhājo hi rājāno jarāsaṃdham upāsate na ca tuṣyati tenāpi bālyād anayam āsthitaḥ
english: Kings who share in his treasury attend upon Jarāsandha — yet he is not satisfied even by that, having adopted a wrong course through childishness.

sanskrit: mūrdhābhiṣiktaṃ nṛpatiṃ pradhānapuruṣaṃ balāt ādatte na ca no dṛṣṭo 'bhāgaḥ puruṣataḥ kva cit
english: He seizes by force a lord of kings, a man of the highest rank — and nowhere have we seen a portion taken from a man without consequence.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvān vaśe cakre jarāsaṃdhaḥ śatāvarān taṃ durbalataro rājā kathaṃ pārtha upaiṣyati
english: Thus Jarāsandha has brought under his control those ranked below by the hundred — how then shall a king weaker than he approach him, O Pārtha?

sanskrit: prokṣitānāṃ pramṛṣṭānāṃ rājñāṃ paśupater gṛhe paśūnām iva kā prītir jīvite bharatarṣabha
english: For kings who have been sprinkled and anointed as victims in the house of the lord of creatures — what joy is there in life, like animals consecrated for sacrifice, O bull among Bhāratas?

sanskrit: kṣatriyaḥ śastramaraṇo yadā bhavati satkṛtaḥ nanu sma māgadhaṃ sarve pratibādhema yad vayam
english: When a kṣatriya dies by the sword, he is honored — should we not all therefore repel the Māgadha king?

sanskrit: ṣaḍaśītiḥ samānītāḥ śeṣā rājaṃś caturdaśa jarāsaṃdhena rājānas tataḥ krūraṃ prapatsyate
english: Eighty-six kings have been gathered; the remaining fourteen, O king — when Jarāsandha has them too, something terrible will come to pass.

sanskrit: prāpnuyāt sa yaśo dīptaṃ tatra yo vighnam ācaret jayed yaś ca jarāsaṃdhaṃ sa samrāṇ niyataṃ bhavet
english: He would attain blazing glory — he who creates an obstacle there, and he who conquers Jarāsandha shall certainly become emperor.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca samrāḍguṇam abhīpsan vai yuṣmān svārthaparāyaṇaḥ kathaṃ prahiṇuyāṃ bhīmaṃ balāt kevalasāhasāt
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Desiring the quality of sovereignty and being devoted to my own interests, how could I send Bhīma through sheer recklessness and brute force?

sanskrit: bhīmārjunāv ubhau netre mano manye janārdanam manaścakṣurvihīnasya kīdṛśaṃ jīvitaṃ bhavet
english: I consider both Bhīma and Arjuna to be my eyes, and Janārdana to be my mind — what would life be for one deprived of mind and eyes?

sanskrit: jarāsaṃdhabalaṃ prāpya duṣpāraṃ bhīmavikramam śramo hi vaḥ parājayyāt kim u tatra viceṣṭitam
english: Encountering the force of Jarāsandha, which is hard to cross and of terrible might — your exertion would end in defeat; what then could be accomplished there?
